# `scope_get_state`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the mount horizontal and equatorial coordinates.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x74f90 (64-bit build; error-then-result fall-through @0x751a8-0x751c0), driver GetHoriCoords @0xee730, GetRaDec @0x698f0 -> mount vtable+368 = ScopeAM5::GetCoordinates @0xeeb20 (sends :GR# and :GD#, parses HMS/DMS, only a -1000 sentinel check; base Scope::GetCoordinates @0x3c150 is an error stub; no J2000/JNow/precession code in the guider) |

Needs a connected mount (315) that reports horizontal coordinates (210). Reads alt and az from the controller (a failure replies with the driver's error code), then adds ra and dec from the same reader as scope_get_ra_dec, so that getter's recovery and tracking-state side branches can run. If only the RA/Dec read fails, the reply carries both an error (the thread error code) and a partial result holding alt and az; a client MUST check for error first. INFERRED units, from the controller reply parsers - alt, az and dec in degrees, ra in hours. ra and dec are passed through from the controller with no precession or epoch conversion (READ); which epoch the controller reports is unresolved. Served by the guider process (TCP 4400); a client on the main command port reaches it through the imager unknown-method relay, which is unavailable to guest-table clients. The native-handler grade below does not describe the relay. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :GA, :GZ.

Side effects: Live query of the connected mount through the native mount layer; no motion or setting change is established. Tier C rests on the supplied native mount query path; other runtime-selected mount implementations are unresolved. The RA/Dec read can also run recovery and update tracking-state bookkeeping.

|---|---|---|---|---|

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |
| 210 | The mount driver does not report horizontal coordinates | `not supported` |
| 315 | No mount is connected | `mount is not connected` |

A failed controller read replies with the thread error code (207 when the RA/Dec reader has no live or cached pair); those codes are not exhausted by this table. An RA/Dec read failure returns that error together with a partial result.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":5,"method":"scope_get_state"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_state","result":{"alt":45.0,"az":180.0,"ra":6.75,"dec":20.5},"code":0,"id":5}
```

Reply, err-315:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_state","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":6}
```
